title: Active and Passive Voice: Introduction — Quiz 101
content:
## Active and Passive Voice: Introduction

Learn how active and passive voice change the focus of a sentence.

### Lesson focus

1. Active voice: People speak English all over the world.
2. Passive voice: English is spoken all over the world.

### Understand the pattern

Active voice normally puts the doer before the verb. Passive voice puts the receiver of the action first and uses a form of be plus a past participle. The tense and the central meaning stay the same; the focus changes.

### Worked answers and explanation

People speak English all over the world → English is spoken all over the world. English becomes the subject. Is agrees with the uncountable noun English; spoken is the past participle of speak. The agent people is unnecessary here.

### Try another

Change: The librarian checks the books every Friday.

### Suggested answer

The books are checked by the librarian every Friday. Books is plural, so the passive uses are checked, not is checked.
